Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  March 5, 2026
The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council Chambers
located on the ninth floor of City Hall on March 5, 2026. Commissioner Denmon called the
meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Ashley Ferrette announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Octavio Padilla -
  District 2, Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4
  Absent:  Vacant - District 3, Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director of Park, Recreation, and Community Services
  Teresa Estrada  Assistant Director
  Marisela Mansour  Human Services Program Manager
  Jack Mooring  Tree Trim Supervisor
  Ashley Ferrette  Staff Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. None.

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Tree Trim Supervisor Jack Mooring reported the following:
Parks Division - Staff are upgrading the burglar alarm and fire protection systems at the Centinela
Adobe. This month, Mariposa Landscapes will begin maintenance of the City’s medians and
parkways. As a result, City staff will shift their primary focus to park maintenance. Graffiti Division
- Last month, staff met with the Inglewood Police Department to discuss graffiti at city parks,
particularly at Edward Vincent Park. Since that meeting, police presence at Edward Vincent Park
has increased, and incidents of graffiti have decreased. Staff are transitioning from manual paper
tracking to iPads to better document graffiti removal activities and improve reporting.
Unfortunately, the transition from paper to paperless tracking has presented some technical
challenges. As a result, staff does not yet have complete graffiti removal data for the month of
February. Tree Division - West Coast Arborist will be finishing the removals behind the tennis
courts at Edward Vincent Park. They have also wrapped up the grid trimming in the four districts,
and the arterial pruning has also been completed. They have started the annual ficus tree trimming
in District 3. City crews have completed the Eucalyptus trimming on Arbor Vitae along with all of
the palm tree pruning on La Brea, Manchester, Prairie and Century Blvd. This will allow for street
maintenance work to be done in preparation for the World Cup without interfering with other
contractors.

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

REPORT - RECREATION. Assistant Director Teresa Estrada reported the following: Easter
Eggstravaganza - Join us on Saturday, March 21, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Edward Vincent Park for
our fourth annual Easter Eggstravaganza. Families will be able to come out and enjoy a host of
activities including, arts &crafts, face painting, story time and a special visit from the Easter Bunny.
Inglewood STEM Fest - This year’s STEM Fest will be held on April 18th from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. This
is a family event that hosts STEM activity stations with Los Angeles professional sports teams, panel
discussions with sports industry professionals, giveaways, and more.

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Program Manager Marisela Mansour reported the
following: Senior Center Activities - Our Senior Center continues to grow, with a diverse range of
exciting presentations and activities planned for this month. On March 4th, H.E.L.P. (Helping Elderly
Live productively) & USC Chan of School of Occupational Therapy will be holding a Q & A – on
physical therapy. On March 5, the first of three Tennis class workshops will be held at Vincent Park.
On March 6, Pacific Brain Health Center will be conducting a presentation on “Dementia
Prevention; Lifestyle Choices That Make a Difference”. On March 12, we will be showing the movie
“Empire State”. On March 16, LA County of Mental Health will conduct a presentation on “Grief
and Loss’’. On March 26, we will have a dance celebrating the quarterly birthdays (January,
February, and March). Elderly Nutrition Program - The Senior Center now serves approximately
475 seniors per week through home-delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate
meals. We have just completed distributing emergency meals to 230+ homebound seniors.
Emergency Meals are important because they provide our homebound seniors with shelf-stable
food assistance to address unanticipated food gaps. Fresh produce is offered every day in
collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank, on the fourth Monday of each month. We will soon
celebrate with special meals in March for St. Patrick’s Day and in April for Easter. The Senior Center
also partners with Los Angeles County to refer seniors to our center for home-delivered meals and
healthy eating workshops. As our weekly program participation continues to climb, we look
forward to serving all our seniors. Senior Transportation - The City of Inglewood’s paratransit
program continues to provide trips to seniors and the disabled community in Inglewood and
Hawthorne. Please note that in observance of the Cesar Chavez holiday on Tuesday, March 31,
2026, there will be no service. Passengers wishing to book a trip for Wednesday, April 1, 2026,
must contact dispatch no later than Monday, March 30, 2026, by 2:00 p.m.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Parks, Recreation, and Community Service Department Director Thomas
Uwal reported the following: Median Beautification - In preparation for the 2026 NBA All-Star
festivities, the Parks Division completed targeted beautification efforts on several highly visible
medians throughout the City, including Century Boulevard and Doty Street. The 2026 NBA All-Star
Game and related events were held February 13–15, 2026, at the Intuit Dome, home of the Los
Angeles Clippers. These beautification enhancements significantly improved the visual appeal of
key entry points and major thoroughfares during this nationally recognized event. Building on this
momentum, the Department will continue improving additional high-visibility medians citywide in
preparation for the upcoming FIFA World Cup, ensuring our community remains welcoming,
vibrant, and event-ready. Parks and Police Department Safety Coordination Meetings - The Parks,
Recreation, and Community Services Department continues to prioritize public safety through
quarterly coordination meetings with the Inglewood Police Department and Protective Services.

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

Our most recent meeting was held on Wednesday, February 4, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. Key topics of
discussion included graffiti abatement, homelessness concerns, and other illegal activities
impacting park facilities. These ongoing meetings are critical, as they allow Parks leadership and
law enforcement personnel to collaboratively assess conditions, share updates, and implement
proactive strategies. This partnership strengthens our collective ability to maintain safe, clean, and
welcoming parks for all residents and visitors. Champions Field Project - Completion Update: The
Inglewood Champions Field Project has been successfully completed. In partnership with the Public
Works Department, our team delivered a fully renovated and modernized athletic field designed
to serve football, soccer, lacrosse, and other programs. Project enhancements include the
installation of new synthetic turf and upgraded perimeter fencing to improve both playability and
site security. The revitalized Champions Field now provides a high-quality, safe, and secure
environment that supports youth and community athletics while protecting the City’s investment
for years to come.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Denmon made mention of the new renovated
restrooms at Darby Park. Since the renovation, there have been no sightings of homeless
encampments. He has also noticed that since the new lighting were installed, there have been no
sightings of coyotes.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the meeting
adjourned at the hour of 6:40 p.m.
